title: Like removal by an unauthorized viewer discloses nothing

cases.note: intro_likes.rs::delete_by_a_viewer_who_lost_access_returns_a_null_count — the author restricts the post after the like; DELETE returns liked=false and like_count=None, serialized as JSON null.
Same test asserts the intro_likes row count is 0 afterwards.
LikeState carries exactly {liked, like_count}; the wire object has no body text, attachment id or author field. The type has no other field to carry one.
intro_likes.rs::liking_an_invisible_post_is_404 — PUT on a restricted post by an unauthorized viewer returns LikeError::Unavailable, status 404.

limitations: The visibility decision is the fail-closed default (VisibilityPolicy::deny_restricted) because WP-04's can_view_intro has not landed in this worktree. Every restricted post is therefore denied to non-authors, which is strictly stronger than the real policy. When WP-04 composes its policy, these cases still hold; only the set of viewers who lose access grows.
